transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rohit Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Stellate - Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Stellate - Infra), Priya Kapoor (Stellate - CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): quick review of cost per token numbers, showed cache on vs off numbers, discussed batching increase from 4 to 16 and impact on p95 latency, next steps to run longer benchmark and provide prompt set.

00:00 Maya Chen: hey everyone, um we'll keep this tight — agenda is cost/econ review and next steps, rohit will jump into the numbers
00:14 Rohit Patel: cool, hi all. quick context, we re-ran the 8k-context throughput test with quantized model v2, two configs: prefix-only cache and full KV cache; numbers at a glance tokens per second and tokens per dollar.
00:31 Lena Ortiz: hey, thanks. we mostly care about tail latency — our SLAs are 300ms p95 for 1k sequences and 1s for 8k. are those numbers still realistic?
00:46 Rohit Patel: yes, so for small seq (average 300 tokens) p95 is 220ms on dedicated pool with batching at 4, tokens/sec/$ sits around 1.8M tokens per dollar — with KV cache on that improves to about 2.6M tokens per dollar for our internal profile. caveat: these are based on continuous batching assumptions and our measured sequence length distro.
01:05 Marco Ruiz: can you repeat, 2.6M tokens per dollar with KV? is that for 8k context as well?
01:12 Rohit Patel: good question. the KV cache gain is most pronounced when there's repetition or shared prefixes; for 8k context with varied prompts we saw about 1.9M tokens/$ with KV enabled — so still better than no-cache which was ~1.2M tokens/$.
01:28 Priya Kapoor: are these numbers comparing hosted vs dedicated? because our procurement is asking about committed vs pay-as-you-go economics.
01:36 Maya Chen: right — the runs Rohit referenced were on a dedicated dev pool (reserved instance) to give baseline for canary. hosted API has slightly different unit costs; we can map both to your usage patterns in the spreadsheet we'll send.
01:50 Rohit Patel: also worth noting batching: we tested batch sizes 4, 8, 16. tokens/sec increased roughly linearly up to 8, then marginal gains at 16 but p95 jumped. example: batch 4 p95 220ms, batch 8 p95 310ms, batch 16 p95 580ms for median-seq workload. so if tail latency is critical you cap batching.
02:15 Lena Ortiz: that matches our intuition. our traffic is spiky during daytime; we are worried about latency spikes during organic bursts. what about adaptive batching?
02:25 Rohit Patel: Redwood runtime supports adaptive batching; it can prioritize latency SLOs and lower batch sizes on demand, or route to lower-cost queued path for non-urgent requests. but adaptive batching reduces tokens/sec/$ vs aggressive batching, tradeoff there.
02:40 Marco Ruiz: can we get a run that simulates our burst pattern? 30s spikes to 3x baseline?
02:45 Maya Chen: yes, that's one of the next steps — Rohit will run a workload that follows your token-per-second histogram. we'll include KV on/off and warm vs cold cache runs.
03:00 Rohit Patel: on caching details — prefix cache (short prefix reuse) gave about 15-25% savings in tokens generated for our test prompts, KV cache (full past key-values reuse for multi-turn) had up to 45% savings in best case. but KV cache has memory footprint and may affect throughput if cache misses cause random access patterns.
03:25 Priya Kapoor: memory footprint — are we looking at a different instance class for KV-heavy workloads?
03:32 Rohit Patel: sometimes yes, we pick kernels and instance types that trade off memory for compute; on dedicated you can choose higher memory GPUs or cluster memory pooling. we'll recommend configs in the spreadsheet.
03:45 Lena Ortiz: one operational question — if we enable KV caching, what's the eviction policy? how long do we keep KV?
03:52 Rohit Patel: eviction is LRU by default, TTL configurable. for long-running multi-turn sessions we recommend a session-scoped TTL of 30 minutes unless you want persistent session cache which we can do but needs tighter controls for data residency.
04:12 Marco Ruiz: speaking of data residency, can you confirm logs and KV not leaving our VPC in private mode?
04:18 Maya Chen: yes, for Private deployment we ship a control plane but data never leaves your VPC; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM and KMS can be customer-managed. we'll share SOC/ISO artifacts.
04:35 Priya Kapoor: ok — procurement will want that.
04:40 Rohit Patel: back to cost math — tokens/sec/$ is a useful metric but we also compute cost per request given your mean tokens per request. for your profile average request is ~850 tokens, current estimate cost per request is $0.0009 on dedicated with KV, $0.0018 without KV — roughly speaking.
05:05 Lena Ortiz: can you send that model? our finance folks want monthly cost projection at 1M requests per month.
05:12 Maya Chen: will do — we'll update the cost sheet with 1M and 5M request scenarios.
05:20 Rohit Patel: also we discovered a micro-optimization — sequence bucketing before batching reduces padding and improves tokens/sec by ~8-12% without hurting latency. it's a configurable option.
05:35 Marco Ruiz: that sounds great, any infra changes needed?
05:38 Rohit Patel: no infra change, it's a runtime-level pre-processing step; we'll include recommended bucket boundaries based on your token histogram.
05:50 Lena Ortiz: earlier you mentioned quantization v2 — is quality impacted vs v1? we noticed a few hallucinations in some dev tests last week.
05:58 Rohit Patel: v2 is 8-bit adaptive quant; in our evals quality delta vs fp16 is minor for most workloads but it depends on prompts. we can run your eval set and report regression rates; if needed we can pin to fp16 for sensitive flows while using quant for bulk cheap workloads.
06:20 Priya Kapoor: what's the fallback behavior if the dedicated pool is saturated? do we fallback to hosted? and how are costs tracked?
06:28 Maya Chen: you can set routing policy: failover to hosted API or to a smaller model variant. cost tracking is per-route; Redwood Console will break down tokens and cost per model and per route so you can audit.
06:40 Marco Ruiz: cool. regarding the benchmark, can you include traces for p50/p95/p99 and also raw token rates? and annotate when cache warm vs cold?
06:50 Rohit Patel: yes, we'll push a zip with logs, metrics, flamegraphs of kernel usage and a CSV for token rates.
07:02 Lena Ortiz: timeline check — we need the numbers to inform a decision by April 6th; procurement wants quote and security docs by then.
07:10 Maya Chen: noted. we'll prioritize the benchmark and the security pack; plan to have everything by 2026-03-31 for internal review so you can meet April 6th.
07:22 Rohit Patel: quick question about latency SLO: you mentioned 300ms p95 for 1k seq — do you want us to optimize specifically for that or for mixed traffic?
07:30 Lena Ortiz: target is mixed but must not breach 300ms p95 for 1k; for 8k we can allow up to 1s p95.
07:40 Rohit Patel: ok we'll tune batch caps and adaptive batching accordingly on the test runs.
07:48 Maya Chen: any other blockers?
07:52 Marco Ruiz: procurement will ask about minimum commit for Dedicated — can you give an estimate of committed commit vs reserved savings?
07:59 Maya Chen: yes, on the sheet we'll show three tiers: pay-as-you-go (hosted), dedicated reserved monthly (20-30% cheaper per token depending on term), and dedicated annual (35-45% depending on size). exact depends on your sustained throughput.
08:15 Priya Kapoor: final question, can we do a short canary with 5% traffic routed to Redwood next week?
08:22 Maya Chen: yes we can run a 5% canary. schedule wise we proposed 2026-04-02 to review canary results.
08:30 Lena Ortiz: sounds good. thanks all.
08:33 Maya Chen: thanks everyone — Rohit will follow up with benchmark plan and data request. will share the cost spreadsheet and security docs. meeting adjourned.
notes: Benchmark to include KV on/off, warm vs cold cache, adaptive batching on/off
Include sequence bucketing to reduce padding
Provide SOC 2 and ISO artifacts plus KMS/forwarding details for private deployment
